lines.beaver: 발표 잘 들었습니다. 연구 배경을 여쭤봐도 될까요?
lines.beaver_en: I enjoyed your talk. May I ask about the background?
lines.beaver_roman: balpyo jal deureotseumnida. yeongu baegyeongeul yeojjwobwado doelkkayo?
lines.learner: 네, 감사합니다. 지방 장터 문화를 탐구했습니다.
lines.en: Yes, thank you. I researched local market culture.
lines.roman: ne, gamsahamnida. jibang jangteo munhwareul tamguhaetseumnida.

lines.beaver_en: Why were you interested in market culture?
lines.en: What I learned while traveling started the research.

lines.beaver_en: What materials did you mainly look at?
lines.learner: 조선 시대 문헌을 먼저 꼼꼼히 읽었습니다.
lines.en: First, I carefully read Joseon-era documents.
lines.roman: Joseon sidae munheoneul meonjeo kkomkkomhi ilgeotseumnida.

lines.beaver_en: Did you also do field trips?
lines.learner: 네, 전국 장터 스무 곳을 직접 답사했습니다.
lines.en: Yes, I visited twenty markets nationwide myself.
lines.roman: ne, jeonguk jangteo seumu goseul jikjeop dapsahaetseumnida.

lines.beaver_en: Did the documents match what you found on site?
lines.en: Mostly, but many things had also changed.

lines.beaver_en: What is your finding in a word?
lines.learner: 한마디로 말하자면 장터는 살아 있는 역사입니다.
lines.en: To put it in a word, markets are living history.
lines.roman: hanmadiro malhajamyeon jangteoneun sara inneun yeoksaimnida.

lines.en: Academia called it practical, solid research.

lines.learner: 새로운 연구 방법론을 제시했다는 의미가 있습니다.
lines.en: It's meaningful in that it proposed a new research methodology.
lines.roman: saeroun yeongu bangbeomnoneul jesihaetdaneun uimiga itseumnida.

lines.beaver_en: Could you tell us your future plans?
lines.en: There are endless topics, so I'll keep researching.

lines.beaver_en: Thank you. I look forward to your work.
lines.en: Thank you so much for your interest.
